[June 2016]

Primary season has finally ended (with the exclusion of Washington DC for the Democrats) and at long last, both Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump's campaigns have garnered enough delegates to earn their party's nominations. Both candidates had hoped to secure their positions much earlier but are glad to have, in fact, made it.

Hillary's campaign stumbled for a time from March until May but Bernie Sanders' popularity faltered after he was caught calling some locals in West Virginia "hicks that need to quit crying about their coal mines." Though Sanders did still manage wins in Oregon and California, he was pummeled in every other state.

Meanwhile, despite a spirited effort by Senator Cruz and much of the Republican party, Trump, too achieved success in the final hour, proudly trumpeting that the establishment had no choice but obey the people's choice and nominate him or risk losing to him in November if they force him to run as a third party candidate.

Talk of a contested convention continues despite the threats and the math. Only time will tell how the conventions will shake out.

This is partially true. Kubrick has stated in interviews that 2001 was intentionally vague so that the viewer could draw their own conclusions about what they witnessed. He refused to tell people what he felt the movie was supposed to mean in order to further this end. So in a sense, all answers that fit the details provided by the film are technically correct, but we may never know for sure exactly what he felt the movie was trying to say.

I think you're missing the point of the violence as well. The apes "evolve" through violence just as Hal does in killing the crew. Ultimately Dude murders Hal. In "The Sentinel," (the source short) the monolith is described as a beacon and a first test for man. I think Kubrick expanded that idea by identifying a goal in these tests; Transcendence rather than direct contact. So when Dude is in the psychedelic sreensaver he's leaving our realm for Whoevers'. When he's in the white room, Dude's presented with his decrepit fate, which he wordlessly rejects. He is then born into his higher state, an infant god. It symbolizes the cyclical nature of creation's relationship to its creator(s).

It isn't just violence. It's tools. There is great attention given to the bone as a tool. Mankind evolves as his tools evolve, until the tools become so evolved that they threaten man (represented in the film by Hal killing the crew). This is a critical point in which man must take the next leap in their evolution or face destruction by their own creation.
